Run a Compiled ODE Model

Source: R/solveODE.R
solveODE.Rd

Integrates a model compiled by cppODE() or cvode() over the time points times. Returns the state trajectory and, when the model was compiled with derivatives, their tangent and Hessian (forward) or the cotangent and curvature of a seeded functional (reverse).

Usage

solveODE(
  model,
  times,
  parms,
  tangent = NULL,
  hessian = NULL,
  fixed = NULL,
  forcings = NULL,
  abstol = 1e-06,
  reltol = 1e-06,
  maxattempts = 50L,
  maxsteps = 1000000L,
  hini = 0,
  roottol = 1e-06,
  maxroot = 1L,
  onFailure = c("stop", "warn", "silent"),
  traceFile = NULL,
  cotangent = NULL,
  curvature = NULL,
  keepStore = FALSE,
  store = NULL,
  sensErrCon = TRUE,
  adjoint = NULL,
  maxOrder = NULL,
  stald = FALSE
)

Arguments

model

A compiled ODE model returned by cppODE() or cvode().

times

Numeric vector of output times, non-empty and finite.

parms

Named numeric vector of initial conditions and parameters. Names must include all of c(attr(model, "variables"), attr(model, "parameters")).

tangent

Optional numeric matrix, the tangent of the inputs; shapes in Details. Default NULL: the identity on the active sensitivities.

hessian

Optional numeric array, the second derivative of the inputs; shapes in Details. Needs a model with attr(model, "deriv2"). Default NULL: the inputs are affine in \(\theta\).

fixed

Optional character vector, sensitivity names held fixed in this call, a subset of attr(model, "dimNames")$sens. Unlike fixed of cppODE() it changes without recompiling. Not with a full or partial tangent. Default NULL.

forcings

Named list of forcing data, one element per name in attr(model, "forcings"): a data.frame with columns time and value, or a two-column matrix. cppODE() and cvode() take the forcing names, this argument the data. A forcing is the monotone cubic Hermite interpolant (PCHIP) of the data points and constant beyond the first and the last point, see forcingValues(). Default NULL.

abstol

Absolute error tolerance. Default 1e-6.

reltol

Relative error tolerance. Default 1e-6.

maxattempts

Maximum number of consecutive step attempts without progress in time before the solve stops with return_code = -4. Default 50.

maxsteps

Maximum total number of integration steps. Default 1e6.

hini

Initial step size; 0 (default) triggers automatic estimation.

roottol

Tolerance for locating root events. Default 1e-6. Under rootfunc = "equilibrate" the solve stops once every \(|\dot x_i| \le \mathrm{roottol}\, |x_i| + \mathrm{abstol}\); on a cppODE() model the test covers the sensitivities as well.

maxroot

Maximum number of triggers per root event. Default 1.

onFailure

How to react when the solver returns a non-zero return code. One of "stop" (default; raise an error with the solver message and no partial results), "warn" (emit a warning and return partial results up to t_reached), or "silent" (return the partial result without any signal).

traceFile

Optional path of a CSV file the step trace is written to. Needs a model compiled with stepTrace = TRUE, ignored otherwise. Default NULL.

cotangent

The cotangent of the outputs, [n_t, n_x] or [n_t, n_x, n_seed]. Required by a model compiled with derivMode = "reverse" or "forward-reverse" unless keepStore = TRUE; an error on any other model. result$cotangent is then \(\sum_{t,i} w_{t,i}\, \partial x_i(t) / \partial \theta\), one column per seed. Default NULL.

curvature

Optional, "forward-reverse" only: the derivative of cotangent along the tangent, [n_t, n_x, n_seed, n_s]. For a cotangent that is the gradient of a functional of the outputs, this is that functional's Hessian applied to the output tangent. Default NULL: the cotangent is constant in \(\theta\).

keepStore

Logical, default FALSE. Return the checkpoints of a reverse solve as $store, for a later solve to reuse through store. The cotangent may then be omitted, and the solve returns the values alone. Only on a cppODE() model compiled with derivMode = "reverse".

store

The $store of an earlier solve of the same model at the same times and parms. The solve then integrates nothing and runs the backward sweep alone. A store from a different point is an error. A store may be reused any number of times. Default NULL.

sensErrCon

Logical. Include the sensitivities, under derivMode = "forward-reverse" the tangents, in the error test and the first step. Default TRUE. FALSE takes the steps and corrector iterations of a value run, up to rounding: cheaper and less accurate, the sensitivities are the derivative of the computed solution, as the reverse mode of "adams" returns; that of "bdf" solves the corrector equations instead. Under "forward-reverse" the step grid does not depend on the directions of the tangent. Needs a model with sensitivities, has no effect under derivMode = "reverse"; a cvode() model takes TRUE only.

adjoint

Optional adjointControl() object for a model compiled with derivMode = "reverse". Default NULL, the same as adjointControl().

maxOrder

Optional upper bound on the order of a multistep method, 1 to 5 for "bdf" and 1 to 12 for "adams". Default NULL, the method's own maximum. An error on "rb4" and "tsit5".

stald

Logical, default FALSE. Stability limit detection for method "bdf": the order drops when the step size leaves the stability region of the current order. See Stepping and error control.

Value

A named list:

  • time: the output times, length n_t.

  • variable: the states, [n_t, n_x].

  • tangent: when attr(model, "deriv") is TRUE, [n_t, n_x, n_s]. The third dimension is named by the active sensitivities or the columns of tangent.

  • hessian: when attr(model, "deriv2") is TRUE, [n_t, n_x, n_s, n_s].

  • cotangent: under derivMode = "reverse" or "forward-reverse", the cotangent of the inputs, [n_x + n_p, n_seed], rows as in a full tangent.

  • curvature: under "forward-reverse", [n_x + n_p, n_s, n_seed], the derivative of each cotangent entry along the tangent. Under the identity tangent the columns are the Hessian of the seeded functional. The order of the last two dimensions is that of a Hessian, not that of the argument curvature.

  • correction: under derivMode = "reverse" with adjointControl(refine = TRUE), length n_seed, named as the seed columns: the first-order change of each seeded functional from the computed trajectory to the one the refined sweep differentiated. Value plus correction is the value whose gradient cotangent is. See The value of the refined sweep.

  • diagnostics: solver statistics, printed by diagnostics(): return_code (0 on success, negative codes as in SUNDIALS CVODE), message, accepted and rejected (step counts), fevals, jevals and setups (right-hand side evaluations, Jacobian evaluations, matrix factorizations), last_dt and last_order (size and order of the last successful step), t_reached, and the model's method, useNDF and, on a cvode() model, backend.

  • trace: with stepTrace = TRUE, a data.frame with one row per step attempt: nst (accepted steps before the attempt), t (time at the end of the step), h (signed step size), q (order), dsm (error test value, the step passes below 1), acnrm and acnrm_state (weighted RMS norm of the local error over all components and over the states alone), tq2 (error constant), gamma and gamrat (step size times the leading coefficient, and the ratio of that product to the value at the last factorization), newton_conv (1 when the corrector converged), mode ("BDF", "NDF", "ADAMS", "ONESTEP", or "CVODE" and "CVODE_event" on a cvode() model), nfe, njev and nsetups (cumulative counters) and setup_reason (what triggered the last factorization). A cvode() model reports NaN where CVODES exposes no value.

  • adjoint: under adjointControl(trace = TRUE), see adjointControl().

  • store: with keepStore = TRUE, an external pointer to the checkpoints.

Details

Dimensions

n_t is the number of output rows, nrow(result$variable): length(times), plus one row for each event inside the window and for the time 0 that includeTimeZero adds. n_x is the number of states, n_p the number of parameters, n_s the number of tangent directions and n_seed the number of cotangent columns.

Derivative arguments and results

A derivative argument and the corresponding result have the same name. tangent and hessian are the first and second derivative in \(\theta\) of the inputs going in, and of the states coming out. cotangent is the gradient of a functional with respect to the outputs going in, and with respect to the inputs coming out. curvature is the derivative of the cotangent along the tangent: that functional's Hessian applied to the tangent, on the outputs going in and on the inputs coming out.

Shapes of tangent and hessian

tangent is the Jacobian \(\Phi'(\theta)\) and hessian the second derivative \(\Phi''(\theta)\) of a reparameterization \(p = \Phi(\theta)\) of the initial states and parameters; the results are then derivatives in \(\theta\). tangent takes one of three shapes, told apart by the row count and row names. hessian has the rows of tangent and two dimensions of length n_s.

  • State-only, [n_x, n_s], rows unnamed or named by the states. The parameter rows are the identity on the active sensitivities, the model's sensitivity names minus fixed. result$tangent[t, , ] has this shape and can seed a following solve.

  • Full, [n_x + n_p, n_s], states first: \(\Phi'(\theta)\) itself. n_s may change from call to call.

  • Partial, [k, n_s] with k < n_x + n_p. The row names, a subset of c(variables, parameters), place the rows; missing rows are zero, so those inputs are fixed.

Run-time fixed takes the state-only shape only. Column names, when given, are the active sensitivity names (state-only) or name the directions \(\theta\) (full and partial); unnamed full or partial columns are named theta1, theta2, and so on.

See also

cppODE() and cvode() for model compilation; solveODEBatch() for many conditions in one call; adjointControl(); forcingValues(); diagnostics() for printing solver statistics. Stepping and error control, Forward sensitivities, Reverse mode: the discrete adjoint and Second derivatives: forward over reverse on the cppDE site; Installation and optional libraries for diagnosing a failing solve.

Examples

# \donttest{
if (codegenAvailable()) {
  ## A forward and a reverse build of one model, compiled together into one
  ## shared object in tempdir().
  eqns <- c(A = "-k1*A", B = "k1*A - k2*B")
  fwd  <- cppODE(eqns, compile = FALSE)
  rev  <- cppODE(eqns, derivMode = "reverse", compile = FALSE)
  compile(fwd, rev, output = "solveODE_examples")

  times <- 0:10
  parms <- c(A = 1, B = 0, k1 = 0.5, k2 = 0.2)

  ## Values and sensitivities at tighter tolerances than the default 1e-6
  out <- solveODE(fwd, times, parms, abstol = 1e-10, reltol = 1e-10)
  out$variable[11, ]
  out$tangent[11, , ]                   # [state, parameter] at t = 10

  ## Only two directions: the tangent seeds the rate constants, one column each
  S <- matrix(0, 2, 2, dimnames = list(c("k1", "k2"), c("k1", "k2")))
  diag(S) <- 1
  solveODE(fwd, times, parms, tangent = S)$tangent[11, , ]

  ## Reverse mode: a cotangent weights the states at every time, and $cotangent is
  ## the gradient of sum(cotangent * x) in the initial values and parameters.
  ## keepStore keeps the forward pass, so each further cotangent costs one
  ## backward sweep.
  first <- solveODE(rev, times, parms, keepStore = TRUE)
  onB   <- cbind(A = 0, B = rep(1, length(times)))
  onA   <- cbind(A = rep(1, length(times)), B = 0)
  solveODE(rev, times, parms, cotangent = onB, store = first$store)$cotangent
  solveODE(rev, times, parms, cotangent = onA, store = first$store)$cotangent
}
#> using C++ compiler: g++ [-O2 -DNDEBUG -w -fPIC -fopenmp]
#>         [,1]
#> A   2.531128
#> B   0.000000
#> k1 -3.787318
#> k2  0.000000
# }
